messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: smart-routing-eval errors spiking in eu-west. 5xx rate up ~8% over baseline, p95 latency up ~400ms for Economy tier. Auto-fallbacks not kicking due to policy TTL mismatch. Investigate and mitigate. (alert id: SR-EU-842)

oncall-dana: on it. pinging SRE and runtime. assigning page.

sre-jerome: I see the alerts — queries to policy-eval service are timing out intermittently leading to stale routing decisions. suspects: load spike + config regen lag.

eng-runtime-leah: pulling traces now. initial look shows slow policy-compile RPCs to config-store (~1.2s) around the same window. KV cache hit rate dropped.

infra-mike: infra dashboard shows a short GPU autoscale wobble in eu-west-2 about 02:10 UTC, but not enough to explain policy RPC timeouts. network latencies between control plane and regional config-store spiked ~200ms.

oncall-dana: customer impact? which tenants hit hardest?

cs-emily: early report from AcmeDocs & PackIt — 3 customers reporting higher response times and some 5xx errors. CS on standby; I can draft messages once we have mitigation.

product-ana: priority is keep hosted API stable. prefer routing toward higher-latency but more reliable pathways, minimize 5xx. cost impact acceptable short-term.

eng-runtime-leah: propose immediate mitigations:
- force-route eu-west requests from Economy->Latency tier (weight shift) for 10m window
- reduce economy-tier per-user QPS to 0.5x (soft rate limit)
- disable experimental locality pinning for active policies in eu-west
We'll canary the weight change for 1% of traffic then ramp.

sre-jerome: +1. Also add temporary aggressive circuit-breaker for policy-eval RPCs so stale results don't produce invalid routes.

infra-mike: I can patch routing-config via admin API. prepping curl now.

eng-runtime-leah: sample patch (canary 1%):
```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/redwood/routing/adjust -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"region":"eu-west","shift":{"from":"economy","to":"latency","pct":1}}'
```

infra-mike: applying canary now.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: routing-adjustment submitted by infra-mike at 02:18 UTC, id RA-993. Monitoring canary.

sre-jerome: telemetry: initial 1% canary looks clean; errors on canary path 0. No immediate regression. ramping to 10%.

eng-runtime-leah: while ramping, applying soft QPS limit to economy in eu-west:
```bash
# soft-limit rule id SLR-77
PATCH /admin/quotas/eu-west/economy
body: {"per_key_qps": 0.5, "mode": "soft"}
```

infra-mike: applied soft-limit. will track token drops and retry behavior.

cs-emily: to CS — letting customers know we've applied temporary traffic shaping to reduce errors, may see higher latency for some calls. ETA for follow-up ~30m.

product-ana: agreed. add note that this is a protective measure to limit 5xx; we expect normal latency to return as fallbacks stabilize.

sre-jerome: telemetry after ramp to 25% shift: overall 5xx rate dropped from 8%->2.1% in eu-west. p95 improved by ~180ms. good. continue ramp to 50% if stable for next 5m.

eng-runtime-leah: also toggled off locality pinning for active sessions in eu-west (experimental flag off). that prevents sticky routing to degraded endpoints.

incident-bot: config-change log: flag locality-pinning -> disabled by eng-runtime-leah (chg id LP-210).

oncall-dana: I'm going to run through checklist and capture mitigation timeline for postmortem. handing off on-call to eng-runtime-leah for next 2 hours.

eng-runtime-leah: taking over. I will continue ramp and watch for secondary effects (cache churn, token bucket exhaustion). tagging infra-mike and jerome.

sre-jerome: note: we observed increased retry attempts from SDKs after soft-limit; increased downstream load by ~6%. watching for cascade. if retries cause new spike, we'll revert quota change and rely purely on weight-shift + CB.

infra-mike: ramp to 50% complete. 5xx steady at ~1.9%. region CPU & network look healthy.

cs-emily: customers notified: initial advisory sent to impacted accounts. awaiting confirmation from AcmeDocs.

product-ana: please keep me posted on cost delta; we may need to cap latency-tier capacity if cost blowout.

eng-runtime-leah: action items logged:
- continue ramp to 100% over next 10m if stable
- monitor retry amplification and adjust client guidance
- investigate root cause: config-store latency + control-plane net spike
- postmortem owner: oncall-dana

sre-jerome: if we see new errors after full ramp, fallback plan: restore policy-eval CB to strict + revert weight shift, enable global-bypass for eu-west to route to us-east.

oncall-dana: handoff ack. handing over docs: https://kibana.redwood/trace/SR-EU-842 and runbook snippet pasted below.
```text
Runbook excerpt:
1) Canary weight shift: admin -> routing/adjust -> pct=1 -> monitor 5m
2) Apply soft per-key QPS limit: admin -> quotas -> set per_key_qps 0.5
3) Disable locality pinning: flags -> locality-pinning=false
4) If errors persist -> global-bypass -> route eu-west->us-east
```

eng-runtime-leah: documented current state in incident log. will update when we hit 100% or roll back.

incident-bot: Incident SR-EU-842: mitigations in progress. current owner: eng-runtime-leah. severity-> S3 (regional impact).

cs-emily: AcmeDocs confirmed degradation resolved for them after ramp to 50%. thank you team.

eng-runtime-leah: ramped to 100% at 02:41 UTC. 5xx down to 0.6% and p95 back within SLO. starting post-incident notes draft and will coordinate postmortem with oncall-dana.

noncall-dana: standing down. leaving postmortem ownership with me. good job all. :thumbsup:
